mechanism_narrative: A lower level of the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) below 1.0% signals accommodative monetary policy that reduces discount rates for equity valuation, producing positive S&P 500 forward 20-day returns as corporate borrowing costs decline.
failure_condition: Rank IC for FEDFUNDS as predictor of 20-day SPX returns remains below 0.03 over any 12-month rolling window, or correlation between FEDFUNDS and SPX returns is not significantly negative (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate (UNRATE) exceeds 4.5%, it indicates labor market deterioration that suppresses consumer spending and corporate earnings growth, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward 20-day returns.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 40% of instances where UNRATE > 4.5, or Rank IC for UNRATE as predictor is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous increases in retail sales (RSAFS) above 470,000 million dollars and housing starts (HOUST) above 1,280 thousand units signal robust consumer and business confidence, driving corporate earnings growth and positive S&P 500 forward 20-day returns.
evidence_refs: doc:BEA Retail Trade and Housing Data
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of instances where both RSAFS > 470000 and HOUST > 1280, or interaction term in regression is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: In periods of high industrial production growth (INDPRO > 105), manufacturing output expansion supports corporate earnings growth, resulting in positive S&P 500 forward 20-day returns as supply chain pressures ease.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 40% of instances where INDPRO > 105, or Rank IC for INDPRO in this regime is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A higher level of payroll employment (PAYEMS) above 145,000 thousand persons indicates strong labor market conditions that boost consumer spending and corporate revenue growth, producing positive S&P 500 forward 5-day returns.
failure_condition: Rank IC for PAYEMS as predictor of 5-day SPX returns is below 0.03 over any 12-month rolling window, or correlation between PAYEMS and SPX returns is not significantly positive (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) exceeds 245, it signals persistent inflation that prompts Federal Reserve tightening, causing equity market sell-offs and negative S&P 500 forward 20-day returns.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 40% of instances where CPIAUCSL > 245, or Rank IC for CPIAUCSL as predictor is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A synchronized expansion in quarterly GDP growth (GDPC1 > 16,800 billion dollars) and industrial production (INDPRO > 103.7) signals broad-based economic strength that supports corporate earnings, driving positive S&P 500 forward 20-day returns.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of instances where both GDPC1 > 16800 and INDPRO > 103.7, or interaction term in regression is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: In a regime of low interest rates (FEDFUNDS < 1.0%) combined with high inflation (CPIAUCSL > 245), monetary policy uncertainty increases market volatility, causing negative S&P 500 forward 60-day returns.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 40% of instances where FEDFUNDS < 1.0% and CPIAUCSL > 245, or Rank IC for the regime condition is below 0.03.
